about: Domaine Saumaize-Michelin sits in Vergisson, a village in the southern Burgundy hills tucked beneath the great limestone cliff of the Roche de Vergisson, which appears on the domaine’s label. Roger Saumaize took over four hectares from his father in 1977; the name joins his own with that of his wife, Christine, née Michelin. Today their children, Vivien (who has made the wines since 2018) and Lisa, lead the estate, around ten hectares of mostly Chardonnay with vines averaging close to fifty years old.

“Sur la Roche” was the domaine’s first purchase, in 1979: a single parcel of about 1.65 hectares on the sunny, south-facing flank of the Roche, on white limestone, with its oldest vines approaching a hundred years. It was long bottled as “Clos sur la Roche” and became a Premier Cru with the 2020 vintage, when Pouilly-Fuissé gained its first classified sites. The estate has been farmed biodynamically since 2005. Grapes are picked by hand, pressed slowly, fermented entirely in Burgundy barrels (about 15% new) and aged a year on fine lees, then bottled unfiltered.

Burgundy writer Bill Nanson, tasting the 2022 at bottling, found it fluid and aromatically expressive, mineral and concentrated, and called it “undoubtedly grand vin.” The importer’s notes describe floral and white-fruit aromas with touches of brioche, and a concentrated palate with zesty lemon and a vibrant, mineral finish. Neal Martin of Vinous rated the 2022 at 91 points.
facts: Single 1.65 ha parcel, south-facing limestone below the Roche de Vergisson; vines up to about 100 years old
Hand-harvested, fully barrel-fermented (about 15% new oak), unfiltered
About one year on fine lees
